body:
The acquisition of Golfzon County by South Korea's Jeju-based resort and golf course operator The Sienna Group appears set to clear its financing hurdle. Raising the 800 billion won (approximately $603.7 million) purchase price had been seen as the biggest obstacle, but the group has now secured Meritz Securities as a financial backer alongside private equity firm CL Asset Management.

According to investment banking sources, The Sienna Group recently formed a consortium with CL Asset Management and is negotiating the acquisition of Golfzon County with the seller, MBK Partners, and other parties. MBK Partners began the sale process in March, appointing Morgan Stanley and Samjong KPMG as lead advisers. The stake on the block is the entirety of MBK's controlling interest in Golfzon County. Through special-purpose vehicle Korea Golf Infrastructure Investment, MBK Partners holds a 58.37% stake in Golfzon County (including convertible preferred shares) and also holds drag-along rights over the stake held by second-largest shareholder Golfzon Holdings.

The key to the deal, as ever, was funding. MBK Partners' proposed enterprise value for Golfzon County is 1.75 trillion won (approximately $1.3 billion), applying a 10.3x multiple to last year's adjusted EBITDA of 170.1 billion won (approximately $128.4 million). After deducting net debt of about 950 billion won (approximately $716.8 million), the equity value is known to be around 800 billion won. The Sienna Group has been viewed as short on financial capacity after successively buying Seragio GC (now The Sienna Belluto) in Yeoju, Gyeonggi Province, and Aekyung Group's Jungbu CC (now The Sienna Seoul CC) last year. Of the 225 billion won (approximately $169.8 million) used to acquire Jungbu CC, 125 billion won (approximately $94.3 million) was reportedly raised by pledging the golf course as collateral.

What changed the picture was CL Asset Management's entry. The PE firm, founded in 2020, recently came under the control of real estate developer Mine 42, which acquired a 90% stake, and drew market attention by recruiting former Woori Bank chief Kwon Kwang-seok as chairman. Meritz Securities then stepped in as lead arranger of the acquisition financing, taking on a major share of the fundraising. Meritz Securities has agreed to underwrite the full 500 billion won (approximately $377.3 million) of acquisition financing, structured as a 350 billion won (approximately $264.1 million) senior loan, a 50 billion won (approximately $37.7 million) revolving credit facility (RCF), and a 100 billion won (approximately $75.5 million) mezzanine loan. It has also agreed to support the consortium's project fund formation.

The remaining roughly 300 billion won (approximately $226.4 million) will be raised by the consortium of The Sienna Group and CL Asset Management. A 100 billion won project fund will be assembled, and about 200 billion won is expected to be contributed as subordinated equity by The Sienna Group using funds from affiliates such as Sienna One, UA Sienna and H3. The consortium plans to obtain a letter of commitment (LOC) from Meritz Securities in November and then sign a share purchase agreement (SPA) with the seller. If the deal closes, MBK Partners will recoup its investment eight years after investing in Golfzon County in 2018.

The Sienna Group is seen as pursuing the deal because it values Golfzon County's position as South Korea's largest golf course network and its operating capabilities. The group, whose main businesses are real estate development and resort operation, expanded into golf by acquiring Jeju CC, Jeju's first golf course, in 2022. "After buying Jungbu CC and Seragio GC, The Sienna Group has had success selling memberships by combining resort membership benefits with discounted golf course access," one IB industry official said. "It sees Golfzon County as a way to expand nationwide and is actively pursuing the acquisition."

The deal is viewed as a bellwether for a reshaping of South Korea's golf course operating market. If the large golf platform MBK Partners has held since 2018 passes to a Jeju-based operator and a PE consortium, observers say a new business model could emerge that combines a membership-based resort business with a nationwide golf course network. Still, with the letter of commitment and fund formation remaining before the SPA is signed in November, changes in financial market conditions are expected to be a variable.
